newsitem.title: USA: Market approach backed to ease Internet gridlock.
newsitem.headline: Market approach backed to ease Internet gridlock.

text.p: An industry advisory group urged local phone companies and Internet access companies Tuesday to get together to resolve problems related to surging Internet usage on the local phone network.

The Federal Communications Commission's council on "network reliability," in a final report, recommended to the agency that market-oreiented efforts be used to resolve Internet gridlock, rather than government-mandated measures.
The group is made of top officials from the telecommunications industry, standard-setting organizations, and consumer and labor groups.

It said concerns over Internet congestion can be minimized through the use of a "template" that identifies issues to be resolved in bilateral talks among Internet service providers and phone companies.
FCC Chairman Reed Hundt said better data is needed on Internet congestion to fully analyze the issue.
"I continue to hear anecdotal reports about the strains that the exploding growth of the Internet is putting on the public switched network, particularly the local group," he said in a statement.
"The plannning tool the council has developed is designed to address this issue, but it is fair to say we do not yet know whether it will resolve the issue," he added.
He added that more attention should be focused on the issue of Internet gridlock.
